ALGER, 24/06/2026 (Algeria Tech) — Mobil: ALGIERS, 06/24/2026 (Algeria Tech) — Mobilis SA, a subsidiary of the Algérie Télécom group, is participating in the 57th edition of the Algiers International Fair (SIA) 2026 with a pavilion dedicated to innovative digital solutions. The event, held from June 23 to 28 at the Casbah of Algiers, highlights the operator's latest technological advancements in connectivity and digital services.
Mobilis déploie un pavillon dédié aux in: Mobilis deploys a pavilion dedicated to digital innovations at SIA 2026
Le géant algérien des télécommunications: The Algerian telecommunications giant, Mobilis SA, is taking part in the 57th edition of the Algiers International Fair (SIA) 2026, held from June 23 to 28 at the Casbah pavilion in Algiers. This exhibition space, entirely dedicated to digital solutions, showcases the latest innovations developed by the operator to meet the growing connectivity and digital transformation needs of individuals and businesses. Among the pavilion's flagship attractions are live demonstrations of new 5G+ offers, secure cloud solutions for public and private institutions, and IoT (Internet of Things) services tailored to the industrial and agricultural sectors.
Le stand de Mobilis, conçu comme un labo: The Mobilis stand, designed as an interactive laboratory, also offers visitors practical workshops led by telecommunications and digitalization experts. These sessions provide a hands-on discovery of the benefits of emerging technologies, such as augmented reality, collaborative workspaces, and cybersecurity solutions tailored for SMEs. The operator highlights its strategic partnerships with local and international players to accelerate the adoption of digital tools within the Algerian economy.
La participation de Mobilis au SIA 2026: Mobilis's participation in SIA 2026 is part of a broader momentum aimed at positioning Algeria as a regional digital hub. With a mobile penetration rate exceeding 120% in 2025 and over 30 million internet subscribers, the country boasts a pool of consumers and businesses eager for tailored technological solutions. The innovations presented by Mobilis, particularly in 5G and IoT, could play a key role in modernizing critical infrastructures, such as energy networks or urban management systems. Furthermore, these technological advancements could help reduce the digital divide across the wilayas by offering accessible services even in underserved areas.
Sur le plan économique, l'adoption massi: From an economic standpoint, the massive adoption of digital solutions by Algerian companies represents a major lever to boost the country's productivity and competitiveness. According to ARPCE projections, the digital services market in Algeria is expected to reach 1,500 billion dinars by 2030, up from 800 billion in 2025. Mobilis, as a historical player in the sector, has a decisive role to play in supporting this transition, notably by training local talent and developing sustainable technological ecosystems. These efforts align with the objectives of the Digital 2030 plan, which aims to make Algeria a continental leader in digital transformation.
Contexte du secteur TIC algérien: Context of the Algerian ICT sector
Le secteur des technologies de l'informa: The information and communication technology (ICT) sector in Algeria is experiencing sustained growth, driven by increased demand for connectivity and digital services. In 2025, the mobile penetration rate reached 123%, with over 55 million active lines, while the number of internet subscribers exceeded 32 million, representing a penetration rate of 72%. These figures place Algeria among the most dynamic African countries in terms of digitalization, with an average annual growth of 8% for the ICT market. The Regulatory Authority for Post and Electronic Communications (ARPCE) plays a central role in regulating and guiding this sector, ensuring fair competition among the operators Mobilis, Djezzy, and Ooredoo.
L'État algérien a consenti des investiss: The Algerian state has made massive investments in digital infrastructure, with a budget of 1,200 billion dinars allocated for the 2022-2026 period. Algérie Télécom, as the incumbent operator, has launched several major initiatives, including the rollout of high-speed fiber optics in 48 wilayas and the launch of commercial 5G in 10 pilot wilayas, including Algiers, Oran, and Constantine. The group has also invested 300 billion dinars in modernizing its data centers and developing sovereign cloud solutions for public administrations. These efforts are part of the Digital Plan 2030, which provides for the widespread rollout of 5G by 2028 and 100% fiber optic coverage of the wilayas by 2030.

Mohamed El Hadi Hocini, PDG de Mobili: Mr. Mohamed El Hadi Hocini, CEO of Mobilis SA, emphasized the importance of this participation in SIA 2026 to showcase the operator's technological advancements. "This exhibition is an ideal showcase to demonstrate how Mobilis contributes to the digitalization of the Algerian economy. Our 5G+ solutions, cloud platforms, and IoT services are designed to meet the current challenges of businesses and citizens," he stated. He also highlighted partnerships concluded with local startups and international players to develop innovative ecosystems in Algeria.
De son côté, M. Brahim Bouzeboudjen, min: For his part, Mr. Brahim Bouzeboudjen, Minister of Post and Telecommunications, praised the commitment of telecom operators to infrastructure modernization. "The ICT sector is an essential pillar of Algeria's economic diversification. The innovations presented by Mobilis and its competitors show that we are on the right track to make our country a model of digitalization in Africa," he affirmed during the exhibition's inauguration.
La participation de Mobilis au SIA 2026: Mobilis's participation in SIA 2026 is part of a global strategy aimed at accelerating Algeria's digital transformation. By the end of the year, the operator plans to launch several innovative services, including a unified cloud enterprise resource planning (ERP) platform, as well as a portfolio of solutions dedicated to the health and education sectors. These initiatives will build on feedback from exhibition visitors, whose expectations regarding digitalization are increasingly demanding.
À plus long terme, Mobilis compte étendr: In the longer term, Mobilis plans to expand its partnerships with the wilayas to develop pilot projects in smart cities and smart agriculture. These projects, which are part of the Digital Plan 2030, could make Algeria a laboratory for technological innovation in North Africa. In addition, the operator plans to invest 50 billion dinars by 2028 to strengthen its 5G infrastructure and extend its fiber optic coverage to 20 additional wilayas.
